articles.title: Evander leads Cincinnati to wild-card win over Griezmann and Orlando
articles.description: FC Cincinnati booked an MLS first-round playoff berth with a 3-1 win that eliminated Antoine Griezmann's Orlando City in a wild-card clash Thursday. Brazilian midfielder Evander scored twice and provided an assist as Cincinnati came from behind following Martin Ojeda's opener at Orlando's Inter.co Stadium. Orlando City crashed out in the wild-card round for the second year running, despite the coup of signing World Cup-winning France striker Griezmann, who arrived in July from Atletico Madrid. The 35-year-old had scored 14 goals with eight assists in just 18 appearances this season, helping his new team climb to an eighth-placed finish. But he missed several chances Thursday, including a glanced header onto the roof of the net deep in stoppage time. Ojeda opened the scoring in the 26th minute, slamming home a through ball from Ivan Angulo. The comeback began with a 43rd-minute penalty. Marco Pasalic pulled Pavel Bucha's shirt from a short corner and Evander buried the penalty low and left. The Brazilian grabbed his brace five minutes after the break. Tom Barlow had a shot well-saved by Maxime Crepeau but reached the rebound first to set up Evander. Evander turned creator in the 85th minute, setting up Samuel Gidi for an effort that curled just inside the far post. Cincinnati will play the regular season-topping Nashville in a best-of-three series beginning Sunday. Their top scorer Kevin Denkey will be fresh, having not played Thursday after just returning from Togo international duty. Lionel Messi's Inter Miami, seeking a second consecutive MLS title, will host the Columbus Crew on Saturday in another Eastern Conference matchup.
